MC	<p>1d80_0b37</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #825217;">Gene A</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #825217;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #825217;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0b6b6e;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #0b6b6e;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0b6b6e;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8b3785;">Gene D</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #8b3785;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b3785;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, acd, +++, acd"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #983f0c;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #983f0c;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983f0c;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0b6b6e;">Gene F</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #0b6b6e;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0b6b6e;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #773da8;">Gene H</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #773da8;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #773da8;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cfh, +++, cfh"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>4232_4ca6</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #983f0c;">Gene B</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #983f0c;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983f0c;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #426b16;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #426b16;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #426b16;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006981;">Gene E</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006981;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006981;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bce, +++, bce"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>76ae_483d</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #426b16;">Gene B</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #426b16;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #426b16;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006497;">Gene E</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006497;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006497;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #963660;">Gene X</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #963660;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #963660;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bex, +++, bex"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>93de_ff59</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #745a0d;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #745a0d;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #745a0d;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006497;">Gene F</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006497;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006497;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8b3785;">Gene H</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #8b3785;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b3785;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cfh, +++, cfh"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>6270_b2f0</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9f3335;">Gene H</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #9f3335;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f3335;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #106d5c;">Gene K</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #106d5c;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #106d5c;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #395ca1;">Gene Y</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #395ca1;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #395ca1;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, hky, +++, hky"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>4bfb_809b</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9f3335;">Gene A</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9f3335;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f3335;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #626206;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #626206;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #626206;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006981;">Gene P</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006981;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006981;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, abp, +++, abp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #626206;">Gene A</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #626206;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #626206;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006497;">Gene F</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006497;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006497;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8b3785;">Gene M</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #8b3785;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b3785;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, afm, +++, afm"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>e643_b4fa</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #983f0c;">Gene E</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #983f0c;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983f0c;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #106d5c;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #106d5c;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #106d5c;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #395ca1;">Gene W</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #395ca1;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9f3335;">Gene C</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #9f3335;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f3335;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #426b16;">Gene D</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #426b16;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #426b16;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #395ca1;">Gene F</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #395ca1;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #395ca1;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cdf, +++, cdf"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>fecb_c792</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9f3335;">Gene A</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9f3335;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f3335;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #626206;">Gene K</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #626206;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #626206;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006981;">Gene P</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006981;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006981;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, akp, +++, akp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>bf28_86ce</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #825217;">Gene D</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #825217;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #825217;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #106d5c;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #106d5c;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #106d5c;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5547c4;">Gene P</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #5547c4;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5547c4;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, dkp, +++, dkp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>7e98_8b31</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #745a0d;">Gene A</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #745a0d;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #745a0d;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #106d5c;">Gene B</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #106d5c;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #106d5c;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #395ca1;">Gene C</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #395ca1;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #395ca1;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, abc, +++, abc"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>94f2_79e4</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #626206;">Gene H</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #626206;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #626206;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0b6b6e;">Gene K</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #0b6b6e;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0b6b6e;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #963660;">Gene X</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #963660;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #745a0d;">Gene E</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #745a0d;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #745a0d;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006497;">Gene F</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006497;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006497;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8b3785;">Gene W</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #8b3785;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b3785;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, efw, +++, efw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>a4da_3ee5</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9f3335;">Gene C</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #9f3335;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f3335;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #106d5c;">Gene P</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #106d5c;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #106d5c;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #395ca1;">Gene R</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #395ca1;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #395ca1;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cpr, +++, cpr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>d1db_af38</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #983f0c;">Gene F</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #983f0c;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983f0c;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #426b16;">Gene K</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #426b16;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #426b16;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #773da8;">Gene Y</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #773da8;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #773da8;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fky, +++, fky"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>d390_5554</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #825217;">Gene M</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #825217;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #825217;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #106d5c;">Gene X</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #106d5c;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #106d5c;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #773da8;">Gene Y</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #773da8;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #773da8;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, mxy, +++, mxy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>71d0_1b28</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #745a0d;">Gene D</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #745a0d;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #745a0d;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006981;">Gene N</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006981;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006981;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #773da8;">Gene P</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #773da8;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #773da8;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, dnp, +++, dnp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>4f62_38fb</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #983f0c;">Gene A</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #983f0c;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983f0c;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #11703e;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #11703e;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #11703e;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006497;">Gene Y</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006497;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006497;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, aky, +++, aky"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>1d80_177b</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #426b16;">Gene E</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #426b16;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #426b16;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #395ca1;">Gene F</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #395ca1;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #395ca1;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #963660;">Gene R</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #963660;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #963660;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, efr, +++, efr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>6483_1174</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #825217;">Gene H</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #825217;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #825217;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0b6b6e;">Gene W</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #0b6b6e;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0b6b6e;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8b3785;">Gene X</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #8b3785;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b3785;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, hwx, +++, hwx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9f3335;">Gene F</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9f3335;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f3335;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #626206;">Gene P</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #626206;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #626206;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #395ca1;">Gene X</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #395ca1;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #395ca1;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fpx, +++, fpx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>5913_1b7c</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #983f0c;">Gene D</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #983f0c;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983f0c;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #11703e;">Gene N</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #11703e;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #11703e;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #395ca1;">Gene X</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #395ca1;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #395ca1;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, dnx, +++, dnx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>9371_4c41</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #426b16;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #426b16;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #426b16;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006981;">Gene H</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006981;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006981;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #773da8;">Gene P</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #773da8;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #773da8;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fhp, +++, fhp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #825217;">Gene A</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #825217;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #825217;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #11703e;">Gene D</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #11703e;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #11703e;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5547c4;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #5547c4;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5547c4;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, adf, +++, adf"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>0076_2893</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #745a0d;">Gene C</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #745a0d;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #745a0d;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #106d5c;">Gene H</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #106d5c;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #106d5c;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5547c4;">Gene R</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #5547c4;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5547c4;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, chr, +++, chr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>7ebf_9b55</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #983f0c;">Gene A</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #983f0c;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983f0c;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #11703e;">Gene F</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #11703e;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #11703e;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #773da8;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #773da8;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #773da8;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, afm, +++, afm"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #626206;">Gene B</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #626206;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #626206;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #395ca1;">Gene J</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #395ca1;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #395ca1;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #963660;">Gene T</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #963660;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>e71a_8085</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #983f0c;">Gene D</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #983f0c;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983f0c;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0b6b6e;">Gene H</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #0b6b6e;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0b6b6e;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #773da8;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #773da8;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #983f0c;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #983f0c;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983f0c;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #426b16;">Gene E</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #426b16;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #426b16;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #773da8;">Gene H</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #773da8;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>46c4_02b2</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #825217;">Gene B</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #825217;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #825217;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006981;">Gene J</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006981;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006981;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8b3785;">Gene W</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #8b3785;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b3785;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bjw, +++, bjw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>14ac_0149</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9f3335;">Gene C</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #9f3335;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f3335;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #626206;">Gene D</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #626206;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #626206;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0b6b6e;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #0b6b6e;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0b6b6e;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cdk, +++, cdk"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>3cbd_2731</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #983f0c;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #983f0c;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983f0c;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #11703e;">Gene M</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #11703e;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #11703e;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5547c4;">Gene W</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #5547c4;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5547c4;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, hmw, +++, hmw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>64aa_6ef2</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9f3335;">Gene A</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9f3335;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f3335;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #11703e;">Gene N</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #11703e;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #11703e;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #395ca1;">Gene R</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #395ca1;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>d399_683a</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #426b16;">Gene D</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #426b16;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #426b16;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006981;">Gene P</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006981;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006981;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8b3785;">Gene R</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #8b3785;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b3785;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, dpr, +++, dpr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>1308_8ba2</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #11703e;">Gene D</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #11703e;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #11703e;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #395ca1;">Gene J</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #395ca1;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #395ca1;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #963660;">Gene T</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #963660;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #963660;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, djt, +++, djt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>30b0_7b33</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #426b16;">Gene A</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #426b16;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #426b16;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006981;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006981;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006981;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #963660;">Gene T</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #963660;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #963660;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, aht, +++, aht"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #745a0d;">Gene C</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #745a0d;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #745a0d;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #106d5c;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #106d5c;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #106d5c;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5547c4;">Gene J</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #5547c4;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5547c4;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, chj, +++, chj"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>d125_2cde</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9f3335;">Gene B</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #9f3335;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f3335;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #11703e;">Gene J</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #11703e;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #11703e;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5547c4;">Gene Y</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #5547c4;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5547c4;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bjy, +++, bjy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>732e_6e18</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9f3335;">Gene J</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #9f3335;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f3335;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0b6b6e;">Gene K</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #0b6b6e;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0b6b6e;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5547c4;">Gene P</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #5547c4;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5547c4;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, jkp, +++, jkp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>4c00_32ef</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #983f0c;">Gene E</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #983f0c;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983f0c;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #426b16;">Gene M</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #426b16;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #426b16;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006497;">Gene X</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006497;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006497;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, emx, +++, emx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>f124_df9d</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #426b16;">Gene E</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #426b16;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #426b16;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006497;">Gene M</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006497;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006497;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #963660;">Gene X</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #963660;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #963660;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, emx, +++, emx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #745a0d;">Gene A</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #745a0d;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #745a0d;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006497;">Gene N</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006497;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006497;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #963660;">Gene W</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #963660;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #963660;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, anw, +++, anw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>84fb_70e2</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #426b16;">Gene D</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #426b16;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #426b16;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006981;">Gene H</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006981;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006981;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8b3785;">Gene Y</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #8b3785;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b3785;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, dhy, +++, dhy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral.
