MC	<p>c6c6_1407</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #983f0c;">Gene B</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #983f0c;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983f0c;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #426b16;">Gene E</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #426b16;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #426b16;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #395ca1;">Gene N</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #395ca1;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #395ca1;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ben, +++, ben"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #745a0d;">Gene B</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #745a0d;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #745a0d;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #106d5c;">Gene D</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #106d5c;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #106d5c;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #963660;">Gene T</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #963660;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #963660;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bdt, +++, bdt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>304c_b9ea</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #745a0d;">Gene F</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #745a0d;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #745a0d;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #106d5c;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #106d5c;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #106d5c;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #395ca1;">Gene N</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #395ca1;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #395ca1;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fhn, +++, fhn"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>a13b_5ad8</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #825217;">Gene A</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #825217;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #825217;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0b6b6e;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #0b6b6e;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0b6b6e;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5547c4;">Gene Y</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #5547c4;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5547c4;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, aby, +++, aby"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>20ab_db55</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9f3335;">Gene D</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9f3335;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f3335;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #426b16;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #426b16;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #426b16;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006981;">Gene X</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006981;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006981;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, dtx, +++, dtx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral.
